title.narrative: Improving the health status of people in and around Pendembu by increasing access to water

description.narrative: This project is designed to contribute to food and livelihood security, water, sanitation and hygiene by increasing community access to these facilities. It will contribute to CAFOD’s Food and Livelihoods Security and the Emergency Preparedness, Response and Recovery thematic programme frameworks – as set out in the CAFOD Sierra Leone and Liberia Country Strategy Paper (2016-2021). The project will be implemented in five communities in Pendembu, Kailahun district, which were heavily affected by Ebola. The outcomes of this project are in line with the Sierra Leonean Presidents’ Recovery Priorities, which is a 12 month plan that includes Water and Agriculture as key sectors. The handmaid sisters are one of the implementing partners of CAFOD and will be working closely with the Health ministry and other relevant stakeholders in Kailahun District during the implementation phase of the project. The project outcomes are as set below: • To increase community and school access to safe drinking water and environmental sanitation: The project will build eight latrines and four wells in five communities and schools across the five selected communities in Pendembu Kailahun District taking into consideration availability of facility and population • To reduce the prevalence of water borne and sanitation related diseases through environmental and personal hygiene promotion: communities and schools will be engaged in discussion on personal and environmental hygiene through community health volunteers and school health clubs during awareness raising campaigns. • Farmers have increased production and income through vegetable cultivation: The project will support farmers in groups, and provide them with seeds and input to improve on their vegetable production within the five villages
